story.titleZh: F1车手预计蒙扎意大利大奖赛体验将“怪异”且“令人困惑”
story.summaryZh: F1车手们预计本周末在蒙扎举行的意大利大奖赛将是一次“怪异”、“令人困惑”且“不太美妙”的驾驶体验。2026年能量受限的新赛车将在蒙扎遭遇迄今最极端的挑战。
story.originalTitle: Slower than Hungary? Why F1 drivers think Italian GP will be 'weird'
story.summaryEn: Formula 1 drivers expect this weekend's Italian Grand Prix at Monza to be a "weird", "confusing" and "not fantastic" driving experience. The energy-limited 2026 cars will face their most extreme challenge yet at the circuit.
detailZh: 一级方程式车手们表示，他们已经为本周末的意大利大奖赛做好了心理准备，在蒙扎赛道驾驶将是一种“怪异”、“令人困惑”而且“不太美妙”的体验。
能量匮乏的2026年一级方程式赛车将面临迄今为止最极端的挑战，而且这会带来一些奇特现象，其程度可能超出在其他赛道上所见到的情况。
从外部来看，一些不同寻常的因素可能并不那么明显，但车手们已经就他们的预期给我们提供了一些见解。
当2026年的一级方程式规则首次在模拟器上进行测试时，蒙扎被证明是赛历中最麻烦的赛道之一。
根据初步分析，人们普遍担心赛车在出弯时速度很快，但随着电池电量耗尽，速度会大幅下降。下降幅度之大，以至于车手们甚至在直道中途就不得不降挡。
对能量管理所做的调整——降低充电上限并限制电能释放——意味着现在直道上的速度曲线已经不同了。
这意味着赛车不会像我们过去看到的那样，从通常的350-360公里/小时的峰值速度下降30-40公里/小时。
相反，赛车的速度会趋于平缓，永远达不到过去那样的高速。
正如小红牛（小红牛）的阿尔维德·林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）所说：“电量就是不够。我们在直道上其实并不慢，只是完全不使用（电能）而已。”
迈凯伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里表示，这种能量匮乏带来的一个奇怪后果是，蒙扎赛道的极速很可能反而比像亨格罗林这样的赛道更低。
“我觉得在我们的模拟器测试中，我们其实在匈牙利的前直道上比在这里还快，”他说，“这说不太通，但更多是因为我们根本没有能量可以消耗。”
模拟器测试显示，车手在主直道中段进入第一个减速弯时可能无需降挡，但在上坡进入阿斯卡里弯的入口处可能需要挂入七挡。
蒙扎周末之前的一个担忧是，由于这条赛道对能量如此匮乏，可能会迫切需要在各处大量使用超级切削（super clipping）技术。
这将意味着进一步降低像莱姆莫弯（Lesmo）和阿斯卡里减速弯（Ascari）这样壮观弯角的挑战性。
但国际汽联（FIA）为这个周末设定的5兆焦（5MJ）能量回收上限意味着超级切削不会太多地被使用，因为回收能量的机会实在非常有限。
正如皮亚斯特里所说："如果回收上限更高，我们就会在各处都使用超级切削，可能在每条直道末端损失30或40公里/小时的速度，但在[5兆焦]回收上限下，超级切削的量是正常或合理的。"
在2026年，F1车手们已经迅速学会了他各种聪明的办法，用现在这些赛车在能量匮乏的赛道上跑出速度。
在某些弯角放慢速度以便回收更多能量，如果这能在随后的直道上带来更多能量，反而可能带来好处。
这种现象在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚赛道达到了极端，因为一些车手发现，在像普雄（Pouhon）这样以前可以超高速通过的弯角提前松油门其实是最好的跑法，或者在某些弯角出弯时不以最大功率加速反而更有利。
一些车手认为蒙扎赛道的布局不提供这种聪明跑法的机会，因为回收能量的机会要少得多。
正如兰多·诺里斯所说：“我认为与斯帕的区别在于，那里有两条大直道，但中间有许多弯角，可以给电池充电，然后全部释放出来。
“不幸的是，这里有两条连续的长直道，而且即使在这两条直道之间也几乎没有任何弯角。所以根本没有能量，也没有动力。你没有充电的机会，所以就是慢。”
在蒙扎跑出一圈好成绩的关键，将是尽可能让电池保持最高的电量状态。
这不仅对排位赛中那些有效的计时圈很重要，对计时开始前的准备工作也同样重要。
由于一级方程式为出圈设定了9兆焦的充电上限，再加上车手需要让轮胎达到合适的工作温度，应该有充分的理由去推进节奏，而不是跑得超级慢。
然而，冷却圈被限制在标准的5兆焦。所以，如果车手在排位赛中采用推进-冷却-推进的策略，那么他们很可能需要跑得超级慢，以避免过早过度充电而触及上限。
“我觉得出圈会很慢，但不会慢得离谱，”他说。
“我认为让人不舒服的会是冷却圈，因为出圈和冷却圈的规则不同。所以，在冷却圈里你会跑得非常慢，以便给电池充电。”
车队和车手需要攻克的关键问题之一，就是如何最好地管理单圈开始阶段的电池电量。
如果在帕拉博利卡弯出弯时为了提升尾速而消耗过多电量，可能意味着你已经烧掉了太多能量，那么在驶向最后一个弯道时就会电量不足。
今年早些时候，车手们不得不琢磨在哪里最佳地提前加速，以便让他们的计时刻进入尽可能理想的状态。
这并不理想，因为这意味着每个人的做法都存在一定程度的不确定性。
作为五月份迈阿密站比赛期间推出的调整方案的一部分，这一功能被自动化了，允许车队通过编程来执行，也就是所谓的“自动K”（auto-K），由车队自行决定电池何时介入。
帕拉波利卡弯的出弯处就是会触发这种情况的区域，这意味着车手可以全油门出弯——但电池只会在预先设定的区域释放能量。
林德布拉德是认为这可能给排位赛带来一些风险的车手之一，因为做飞驰圈的赛车和即将开始飞驰圈的赛车之间可能存在很大的速度差。
“我们在赞德沃特稍微见识过一点，但靠着倾斜弯道，问题不大，”他说。
“当时的速度差有50到60公里每小时，所以你可以让开道路，让其他车手过去。
“现在的速度差甚至更大，这可能会变得有点危险。所以，开始飞驰圈并不容易，要做到满电输出、让轮胎进入状态。
“但即便只是从交通状况和安全性来看，这也不太好。我们需要更好的电池。”
detailEn: Formula 1 drivers have talked about being braced for a “weird”, “confusing” and “not fantastic” experience in driving Monza for this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix.
The energy-starved 2026 F1 cars are going to face their most extreme challenge so far, and it is going to throw up some quirks that may be a step beyond what has been witnessed at other venues.
From the outside, some of the unusual elements may not be so obvious, but drivers have already offered us some insight about what they expect.
When Formula 1’s 2026 regulations were first tried out on simulators, Monza proved to be one of the most troublesome tracks on the calendar.

Based on initial analysis, fears were widespread of cars blasting out of the corners and then speeds falling away as the battery power ran out. The drop-off was such that drivers were even having to change down gears halfway down the straights.
The tweaks that have been made to energy management – in reducing recharge limits and capping deployment – have meant the speed profile down the straights are different now.
It means that the car will not actually be suffering a 30-40km/h speed drop-off from the typical 350-360km/h peaks we have seen in the past.
Instead, they will flatline to never get near the old highs.
As Racing Bulls’ Arvid Lindblad said: “There's just not much battery. We don't actually go slower on the straights. We just don't use any.”
McLaren’s Oscar Piastri said that one of the bizarre consequences of the energy starvation was that top speeds would likely be lower at Monza than at a track like the Hungaroring.

“I think in our sim running we were actually quicker on the front straight in Hungary than we were here,” he said. “It doesn't make a whole lot of sense, but it's more that we just don't have the energy to spend.”
Sim running suggests drivers may not need to change down gears halfway down the main straight into the first chicane, but they may need to slip into seventh on the uphill entry to Ascari.
One of the fears ahead of the Monza weekend was that, because it was so energy starved, there could be a desperate need to super clip everywhere.
This would have meant further reducing the challenge of spectacular corners like the Lesmos and the Ascari chicane.
But the 5MJ harvesting limit that the FIA put in place for this weekend means that super clipping is not going to be called upon much, as opportunities to recover energy are so limited.

As Piastri said: “If the harvest limit was higher, we would be super clipping everywhere, probably losing 30 or 40 km/h at the end of each straight, but with the [5MJ] harvest limit, the super clipping is a normalish amount, or a reasonable amount.”
F1 drivers have learned quickly in 2026 the various clever ways to be quick at energy starved tracks with these current cars.
Being slower through some corners to help harvest more energy can deliver benefits if it delivers more energy on subsequent straights.

This is something that reached extremes at Spa-Francorchamps, as some found that lifting off in previously super-fast corners like Pouhon was actually the best way to go, or not accelerating with maximum power coming out of some corners was beneficial.
Some drivers think that the layout of Monza does not offer the opportunity for such a smart approach, as the chances to recover energy are much less.
As Lando Norris said: “I think the difference to Spa was that you had two big straights but you had lots of corners in-between that you could charge up and then deploy everything.

“Unfortunately here you have two long straights back-to-back, but even between them there's not really any corners. So, there's just no energy, there's just no power. You don't have an ability to charge, so it's just slow.”
The key to a good lap around Monza is going to be about maximising the state of charge of the battery.
This matters not only for laps that count in qualifying but also for preparations before the timing gets underway.

With F1 setting a recharge limit of 9MJ for out-laps, plus a need for drivers to get their tyres up to the right operating temperature, there should be every reason to push on rather than go super slow.

However, cool-down laps are capped at the standard 5MJ. So, if a driver is on a strategy of push-cool-push in qualifying, then the likelihood is they may need to go super slow to risk not over-charging early on and hitting the ceiling.
“I think the out-laps will be slow, but I don't think they'll be stupid,” he said.

“I think what won't be enjoyable is going to be cooldown laps, because the rules are different between out-laps and cool laps. So, in cool laps you'll be going very slow to try to charge the battery.”
One of the key aspects that teams and drivers are going to need to get on top of is how best to manage the battery for the start of the lap.
Deploy too much for a top speed boost out of Parabolica and it could mean you have burned too much energy, so you are left short on the run to the final corner.
Earlier in the year, drivers had to work out where best to accelerate before the timing line to start their laps in the best place possible.
This was not ideal as it meant there was a certain level of unpredictability about what everyone was up to.

As part of the package of in-season tweaks pushed through for Miami in May, this was automated to allow teams to execute this through programming of what’s become known as ‘auto-K’ where teams decide when the battery kicks in.
The exit of Parabolica is an area where this will take place, so means drivers will exit flat on the throttle – but the battery will only deploy in an area that is predetermined.
Lindblad is one who thinks this could pose some risks in qualifying if there is a major speed offset between cars on quick laps and those who are about to start.
“We saw it a bit in Zandvoort, but it was okay because of the banking,” he said.
“There was a 50-60 km/h speed delta, so you could get out of the way and let the guys through.
“Here it's even more - and it could become a bit dangerous. So, starting the lap won't be easy, to have it full, have the tyres ready.
“But even just from traffic, from safety, it's not great. We need a better battery.”

relatedItems.titleZh: 博塔斯解释巴库站大幅落后佩雷兹的原因
relatedItems.summaryZh: 博塔斯透露，在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上他平均每圈比凯迪拉克队友佩雷兹慢超过1.7秒，是2026赛季迄今正赛中最大的队内差距，他对此表示在直道和弯角都无法跟上节奏。
relatedItems.originalTitle: The slowest race of F1 2026 explained
relatedItems.summaryEn: Valtteri Bottas has revealed why he was on average more than 1.7 seconds per lap slower than his Cadillac team-mate Sergio Perez at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the largest race-day intra-team deficit of the 2026 season so far.
detailZh: 瓦尔特里·博塔斯透露了上一站巴库比赛中，他相比凯迪拉克F1队友塞尔吉奥·佩雷兹速度严重不足的一些原因。
在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上，博塔斯平均每圈比佩雷兹慢超过1.7秒之多，这是2026赛季迄今正赛中最大的队内差距。甚至他的最快单圈也比佩雷兹慢1.489秒。
博塔斯在最后一圈撞上护墙，因为他在驶过1号弯逃生通道后，赛车的能量输出模式“有点混乱”，而由于多跑了距离，他在进入15号弯左弯时后刹车失效，车头撞上了护墙。
但更令人担忧的是此前惊人的速度差距，在博塔斯撞车之前，佩雷兹几乎已经套了他一圈。
“我理解从外面看起来情况很糟糕，坐在车里感觉也很糟糕，”博塔斯周四在马来西亚说。
“当时根本没办法跟上大部队。我在比赛中尝试了所有办法，也得到了很多关于我在哪里损失时间的反馈。很大一部分是在直道上，但也有相当大的一部分是在整圈的弯道中损失掉的。
“所以我一直在坚持推进直到最后，这也是为什么我在最后一圈进一号弯时锁死了轮胎。
“不过是的，关键问题是在练习中我们就已经看到我的速度不够。我无法像佩雷兹那样以同样的速度过弯，所以我们在排位赛前做了很多改动，包括一些减震器和底板，结果感觉确实好多了。
“但在正赛中，行驶品质又明显衰减了很多……我们这次改动了很多东西，所以我觉得问题在于减震器随温度衰减，还有底板……我们在某些地方仍然缺少一些压力测量点，所以对于气动部件，我还拿不到过去习惯获得的完整信息。
“通过数据你马上就能看出性能是提升还是下降，但现在底板有一些区域我们完全看不见。不过就我个人的感觉而言，更多问题出在行驶品质上——再加上动力转向整个周末都在不断衰减。所以我在整场比赛中真的很难去感受赛车。
“这些因素叠加在一起。而且动力单元的差距可能比我们预想的要大，至少从数据上看是这样。
“理论上我们有一个数字，但那是新引擎对全新引擎，也就是新规格对旧规格的对比。所以，我想就是这些因素叠加的结果。我当时确实相当慢。”
动力单元方面的差异指的是佩雷兹在巴库已经用上了升级版 ADUO 2 法拉利引擎，而博塔斯还没有。
此前这被描述为“细微差别”，但正如博塔斯所说，这次升级的效果可能比最初想象的更大。
博塔斯表示，他的 ADUO 2 引擎能否及时送到、让他能在雪邦赛道使用，可能性是“五五开”；如果赶不上，他就得等到下周的新加坡大奖赛。
他的队友佩雷兹本周末不会使用这套引擎，而是换用自己引擎池中的另一套动力单元，以便把升级版留到更能发挥作用的比赛周末再使用。
佩雷斯解释说：“我们做出了一个我们认为胜算最大的决定。”
“这就是为什么我们会在这里承受一些损失。但我们希望这会有所回报。”
“我们对这个周末并不太乐观。所以我们决定把它省下来。”
正如佩雷斯所暗示的，凯迪拉克的车手们已经为艰难的周末做好了准备，因为雪邦赛道带来了两个凯迪拉克尤其难以应对的挑战：轮胎过热和高速弯角。
正如佩雷兹所解释的，凯迪拉克目前“赛车的下压力严重不足，而且阻力很大”。
“在巴库，我基本上整场比赛都保持在超车模式上，所以才能跟住其他车手，”佩雷兹说。
“但当我超过他们之后，我就只能像个乘客一样，因为我没有直道速度。所以我们有两大问题：下压力不足和很大的阻力。”
“但我们一直都知道，第一年会很艰难。”
detailEn: Valtteri Bottas has revealed some of the reasons behind his woeful lack of pace compared to Cadillac Formula 1 team-mate Sergio Perez last time out in Baku.

Bottas was on average over a whopping 1.7 seconds slower than Perez per lap at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the largest race day intra-team deficit of 2026 so far. Even his single fastest lap was 1.489s slower than Perez.

Bottas ended up in the wall on the final lap as his car’s deployment pattern “got a bit confused” because he went down the Turn 1 escape road, then because of the extra distance travelled his rear brakes didn’t work going into the Turn 15 left-hander, where he nosed into the barriers.
But what was more worrying was the alarming lack of pace before then, with Perez close to lapping Bottas before the latter's crash.
“I understand it looked pretty bad from the outside and felt pretty bad in the car as well,” Bottas said on Thursday in Malaysia.

“There was just no way to keep up with the pack. I tried everything during the race, and got lots of feedback on where I am losing the time. A lot of it was on the straights, but also a big chunk was just all around the lap in the corners.
“That's why I just kept pushing until the end and that's why I had to lock up on the last lap into Turn 1.

“But yeah, the main thing was we saw already in practice that I was lacking pace. I couldn't carry the same speed through the corners as Checo, so we changed a lot for the qualifying, including some dampers and the floor, and it actually felt a lot better.

“But then the ride again during the race degraded quite a lot... Again, we've changed a lot of things, so I think it's something to do with dampers degging with heat, the floor... We are still lacking a bit of pressure tappings here and there, so we still don't have the full information on aero parts that I'm used to from the past.

“You can immediately see if you're down or up, but now there are some bits of the floor where we are blind. But for me, feeling-wise, it was more the ride - that, in combination with the power steering that was degging throughout the weekend. So I was really then also struggling to feel the car throughout the race.
“So those things combined. And then the [power unit] difference was probably bigger than we thought, at least from the data.
“We've got a number in theory, but that's new engine versus new one, of the new and old spec. So yeah, I think those combined. I was pretty slow.”
The power unit difference is in reference to Perez having the upgraded ADUO 2 Ferrari engine in Baku while Bottas doesn’t yet have it.
This was previously described as a “small difference”, but as Bottas says the upgrade may be more powerful than first thought.
Bottas says it’s “50/50” if his ADUO 2 engine arrives in time for him to run it at Sepang; if not, he’ll have to wait until next week in Singapore.
Team-mate Perez won’t be running it this weekend, swapping to a different power unit in his pool in order to save it for a weekend when it will be more beneficial.
“We took a decision where we feel we got the best shot at it,” Perez explained.
“That's why we're taking a bit of a hit here. But we hope that it will pay us back.
“We are not too optimistic about this weekend. So we decided to save it.”
As Perez alluded, the Cadillac drivers are braced for a difficult weekend because Sepang poses two challenges the Cadillac struggles with in particular: tyre overheating and high-speed corners.
As Perez explains, the Cadillac has “a massive lack of load in the car and a lot of drag” right now.
“In Baku, I basically stayed on the overtake mode for the entire race and therefore I was able to stay with the others,” Perez said.
“But when I overtook them, I was just a passenger because I had no straightline speed. So we have two big issues: load and a lot of drag.
“But we always knew this first year was going to be tricky.”
keyPointsZh: 博塔斯的最快单圈也比佩雷兹慢1.489秒

keyPointsEn: Bottas's fastest single lap was still 1.489s slower than Perez's

relatedItems.summaryZh: 埃斯特班·奥孔离开哈斯车队时再度提及“超出自己控制的因素”，暗示这段车手与车队关系的逐渐恶化。哈斯早在夏休期后便通知奥孔大概率不会留队，而法拉利支持的青训车手拉法·卡马拉被认为是接替他的热门人选。
relatedItems.originalTitle: All the reasons the Ocon-Haas relationship fell apart
relatedItems.summaryEn: Esteban Ocon marked his exit from Haas with another reference to elements beyond his control, hinting at a gradual deterioration of the driver-team relationship. Haas decided long ago not to activate its contractual option and informed Ocon shortly after the summer break that he was unlikely to be retained.
keyPointsZh: 哈斯拥有下赛季保留奥孔的合同选择权，但早已决定不激活，并在夏休期后不久通知了他。
法拉利支持的拉法·卡马拉是最热门的接替人选，有人推测是法拉利对其青训车手的支持将奥孔挤出车门。
签约时奥孔是哈斯自2016年车队成立赛季引进罗曼·格罗斯让以来拥有的最成功车手。
keyPointsEn: Haas had a contractual option to retain Ocon for next year, decided long ago not to activate it, and notified him shortly after the summer break.
Ferrari-backed Rafa Camara is the favourite to replace Ocon, leading some to infer Ferrari's support of its junior driver is pushing Ocon out.
When signed, Ocon was the most successful driver Haas had employed since Romain Grosjean, a 10-time podium finisher who joined for the team's inaugural 2016 season.

relatedItems.titleZh: 马来西亚大奖赛回归在即，车手期待雪邦或将上演混乱激战
relatedItems.summaryZh: 阔别近十年后，F1将于2026年重返雪邦，替代被取消的巴林和沙特大奖赛，车手们对这条久未造访的赛道展开了各自的预测。
relatedItems.originalTitle: 'Chaotic racing'? - What F1 drivers expect from Malaysia return
relatedItems.summaryEn: Formula 1 will return to Sepang in 2026 after nearly a decade away, replacing the cancelled Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, and drivers have been sharing their early predictions about the challenge ahead.
keyPointsZh: 大部分车手在阿塞拜疆-马来西亚-新加坡三连赛开始前已在模拟器上为雪邦做了准备
威廉姆斯的模拟数据显示，雪邦在2026年赛道中的能源管理需求约为中等水平，与加拿大和奥地利站相近
世界冠军兰多·诺里斯曾在2017年为迈凯伦车手阿隆索和范多恩担任模拟器支持工作
keyPointsEn: Most drivers had already completed simulator preparations for Sepang before the Azerbaijan-Malaysia-Singapore triple header began
Williams's data places Sepang around average in energy management demands for 2026 circuits, similar to Canada and Austria
World champion Lando Norris provided sim support for McLaren's race drivers Fernando Alonso and Stoffel Vandoorne the last time F1 raced there in 2017
